subject: Request: CAIQ / SOC2 - Ephemeral log sample & key-rotation exception
messages:
From: Audrey Li <audrey.li@hexwell.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Hexwell Security Team <security@hexwell.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CAIQ / SOC2 follow-up - ephemeral logs and key rotation

Hi Priya,

Thanks for taking the time on the call last week. As part of our vendor assessment for Hexwell's SOC 2 scoping, we need two items to complete the CAIQ mapping: a short sample (redacted) of ephemeral access logs showing prefix/KV cache writes for a 24-hour window, and documentation of your KMS rotation cadence plus evidence of the last rotation event.

We understand some artifacts are sensitive — if there is a standard exception path for ephemeral/short-lived credentials or you can provide a hashed/indexed sample that preserves provenance, that will work. Could you upload to our Archer portal request (link below) or share via a secured link? Goal is to close the CAIQ control items by 5/9.

Portal: https://archer.vendorportal.com/requests/47291

Attachments: CAIQ checklist (we already pre-filled some answers during the call).

Appreciate a point of contact and ETA.

Best,
Audrey Li
Senior Vendor Security Analyst
Hexwell Technologies

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Apr 2025 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: CAIQ / SOC2 follow-up - ephemeral logs and key rotation

Kimberly / Marcus — forwarding Hexwell's ask. Two deliverables: (1) a 24-hour redacted sample of ephemeral access logs that show KV cache/prefix write activity, and (2) KMS rotation evidence (last rotation event + policy cadence). Hexwell said a hashed/indexed sample is acceptable.

Action items: 
- Kimberly: can you pull a 24-hour sample from the production access logs and redact IPs/UUIDs where needed? Output should preserve timestamps and event types (e.g., CACHE_WRITE, KVCACHE_EVICT). Format as JSON lines or CSV.
- Marcus: please prepare a 1-page KMS rotation summary (who/when/how) and point to the last rotation artifact. If there is a signing cert or rotation ticket in Jira, include the reference.
- Vanessa: once we have both artifacts, can you stage the upload to Archer and mark the CAIQ controls we mapped as 'evidence attached' so their portal reviewer sees it?

I've attached a portal prefill we can use to double-check mapping and a CAIQ delta worksheet to track which controls are still open. ETA: can we aim for draft artifacts by 4/30 EOD? Hexwell's deadline is 5/9 so we want buffer.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Security Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachment: portal_qna_prefill.json (stub)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Apr 2025 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: CAIQ / SOC2 follow-up - ephemeral logs and key rotation

On Mon, Apr 28, 2025 at 10:04 AM Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Kimberly / Marcus — forwarding Hexwell's ask. Two deliverables: (1) a 24-hour redacted sample...

Quick update: I pulled a 24-hour slice (2025-04-25 00:00 - 23:59 UTC) of access events from the inference-serving cluster's audit stream. I will redact PII and replace UUIDs with deterministic hashes so Hexwell can still verify event ordering. Sample will include event_type, timestamp, truncated_request_path, and cache_op (CACHE_HIT/CACHE_WRITE/CACHE_EVICT).

Question: Hexwell explicitly asked to show 'prefix/KV cache writes' — our internal labeling is 'cache_op: CACHE_WRITE' in the audit stream but not every write includes the prefix name. Do you want me to include the (redacted) prefix identifiers or just the op types and counts?

I can deliver a ~200-line JSONL sample and a short README explaining redaction rules. Targeting 4/30 AM upload to a secured S3 presigned link, then Vanessa can put to Archer.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Sr. Security Engineer, Platform
Redwood Inference
Attachment: sample_redaction_readme.txt (stub)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 May 2025 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: CAIQ / SOC2 follow-up - ephemeral logs and key rotation

On Wed, Apr 30, 2025 at 08:37 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com> wrote:
> I pulled a 24-hour slice...

Thanks Kim — include the redacted prefix identifiers (hashed) so Hexwell can see ownership of the namespace without seeing the raw keys. I'll draft the KMS rotation summary: cadence is quarterly, last scheduled rotation 2025-03-12. Evidence: rotation was executed via ticket INFRA-1987 and a rotation artifact (kms-rotation-20250312.sig) lives in our secure evidence bucket. I'll export the short PDF summary and include the Jira ticket link and artifact filename.

Vanessa: once Priya confirms, stage both artifacts to Archer under request 47291 and set visibility to 'security-review-only'. Also flag the CAIQ control items we closed in the delta mapping.

Marcus Lin
Director, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference
Attachment: kms_rotation_summary.pdf (stub)
From: Audrey Li <audrey.li@hexwell.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Hexwell Security Team <security@hexwell.com>
Date: Fri, 02 May 2025 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ / SOC2 - Ephemeral log sample & key-rotation exception

Priya / team — thanks for the quick turnaround. We received the sample and the KMS rotation summary in Archer (request 47291). A couple notes from review: the hashed prefix IDs are sufficient and the redaction README is helpful. We marked CAIQ controls SC-3.1 and KeyMgmt-2 as 'evidence accepted, reviewer note: confirm automations for quarterly rotation' — can you attach the Jira rotation automation runbook or confirm the scheduled job name?

If you prefer, we can accept a short exception path for ephemeral keys that explains retention, access, and deletion windows — DocuSign acknowledgement would suffice for Hexwell compliance. If you want to pursue the exception, I'll send the DocuSign link.

Next steps: Priya, please attach the runbook (or job name) and let us know by 5/6 if you want the formal exception path. Otherwise, thanks — will close the CAIQ items pending that confirmation.

Best,
Audrey Li
Senior Vendor Security Analyst
Hexwell Technologies
Attachment: reviewer_notes.txt (portal comment)
